memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If a bull gores a man or woman to death, the bull is to be stoned to death, and its meat must not be eaten. But the owner of the bull will not be held responsible. If, however, the bull has had the habit of goring and the owner has been warned but has not kept it penned up and it kills a man or woman, the bull is to be stoned and its owner also is to be put to death." - Exodus 21:28-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's justice weighs what we knew and what we did with that knowledge. If a bull suddenly gored someone, its owner was not blamed — how could he foresee it? But if that bull had gored before, if the owner had been warned and still did nothing, then the tragedy was on his hands. Knowledge brings responsibility. To be warned and ignore it is a serious thing.

There is a quiet lesson here for all of us. We often know exactly where the "dangerous bull" is in our lives — the temper we refuse to fence in, the habit we keep excusing, the sin we have been warned about again and again. God does not treat repeated, knowing negligence lightly. What we permit, we are responsible for.

But this is not meant to crush us; it is meant to wake us up. God warns us precisely because He loves us and wants to spare us and others from harm. Today His Spirit may be pointing at something you have long known about but kept "unpenned." Grace does not ignore it — grace gives you the power to finally deal with it. Do not wait for tragedy to take seriously what God has already flagged.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
What "dangerous bull" have I been warned about but left unpenned in my life?
How can I take responsibility for it today rather than waiting for harm?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for warning me out of love. Give me the honesty and courage to deal with what I have long ignored, before it brings harm to me or others. Amen.
